title: Musher Component Document
description: A reusable, versioned definition of one graph node: a workload this platform runs (its source, lifecycle, endpoints, storage and health) or an external node it does not, and the configuration contract either consumes and publishes.
$comment: Structural and type validation only — cross-document reference resolution, slug/directory agreement, and platform capability checks are separate validation layers. See spec.md.

kind.description: Document kind discriminator. Must be COMPONENT.

specVersion.description: Version of the Musher specification this document is written against.

ComponentBuild.$comment: spec.md §5.1. Exactly one of dockerfile and buildpacks says how the source is built; arguments apply to either.

arguments.description: Build arguments keyed by argument name, injected into the image build context (Docker ARG). Build-time configuration only; runtime configuration rides on the workload's envVars and inputs.

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §5.1 / ADR 0007 §4. A build argument becomes an environment variable in the build context, so it takes the environment-variable grammar rather than one of its own.

dockerfile.description: Build with a Dockerfile, at this path relative to the repository root.

baseURL.description: Existing input receiving the connection baseURL role.

apiKey.description: Existing input receiving the connection apiKey role.

model.description: Existing input receiving the connection model role.

protocol.description: Required client protocol, independent of upstream vendor.

capabilities.description: Required protocol features. Omission requires no optional capabilities.

inputs.description: Typed input declarations keyed by input name.

outputs.description: Typed output declarations keyed by output name.

connectionRequirements.description: Atomic connection requirements; each member input has exactly one owner. See spec.md §6.4.

protocol.description: Protocol served on the port: HTTP, HTTPS, WS, GRPC, TCP, or UDP.

targetPort.description: Port the workload listens on, where traffic for this endpoint is forwarded. Never the public port, which the platform allocates. A port below 1024 is structurally valid; admission may reject it as a capability check.

ComponentGitRef.$comment: spec.md §5.1. Exactly one of branch and commit.

branch.description: Branch to build from. A request, not a pin: the branch moves.

commit.description: Commit to build from. Identifies source, not every build input.

build.description: How the repository is built into an image. Required: a Git source has no image until something builds one, and leaving the strategy implicit makes the resulting image depend on the builder rather than on this document.

ref.description: Branch or commit to build from. Omitted, the repository default branch.

repositoryURL.description: Git repository URL the platform builds into an image.

ComponentHealthProbes.description: Staged health probes: startup, readiness, liveness.

liveness.description: Aliveness gate; failure restarts the workload. Optional.

readiness.description: Traffic gate; failure pulls the replica from routing without a restart. Required for a SERVICE exposing a public endpoint.

startup.description: Initialization gate; failure means not-yet-started. Optional.

ComponentHttpProbe.description: An HTTP request the platform sends; a 200 to 399 status succeeds.

endpoint.description: Named endpoint serving HTTP or HTTPS.

path.description: Absolute HTTP path the platform requests.

ComponentImageReference.$comment: Lookahead-free so it compiles under RE2 as well as ECMA-262. The tag colon is the one after the final slash, which is what keeps a registry port (localhost:5000/nginx) from reading as a tag. Only the grammar is here: the floating-tag blocklist stays a semantic rule. See spec.md §5.1.
ComponentImageReference.description: OCI image reference the workload runs from. Must carry a tag or an @sha256 digest; a bare name is an implicit :latest and shifts under the registry.

description.$comment: spec.md §6 COMP-DESC-001. REQUIRED, and the component is its only home: a blueprint parameter carries no description of its own and shows this one, so a value is described once, by the document that needs it.

required.description: Whether absence is forbidden; defaults to true.

target.description: Environment destination; required on workload inputs.

sensitive.description: True when the value is secret material: handled as a secret reference, masked in UIs, never echoed back.

presentationHint.description: Optional presentation annotation, not a value constraint.

default.description: Logical fallback used only when no binding is declared.

envVarKey.description: Environment variable the resolved value is bound into at runtime materialisation (e.g. ADMIN_EMAIL). Uppercase letters, digits, and underscores; must not start with a digit.

ComponentMetadata.description: Identity and description of a component document. The name is the file stem.

description.$comment: spec.md §4 COMP-DESC-002. Plain text, never rendered as Markdown, and bounded like a listing summary: it is one or two sentences a composer reads beside a node, not documentation. Structurally optional so a component can be stored while it is being written; COMP-DESC-003 requires it of a published one.
description.description: What this component is, in one or two plain-text sentences. Required to publish.

revision.description: Lineage revision of this component. Required (never defaulted) so the component's content is a pure function of this file, and it is the revision the item's blueprint nodes pin.

sensitive.description: True when the value is secret material: handled as a secret reference, masked in UIs, never echoed back.

ComponentOutputFrom.$comment: spec.md §6.2 / ADR 0031 §1. Where the output value comes from is the key that is present: a literal value, one of this component’s own inputs, a property of one of its endpoints, or a template over its own endpoints. Exactly one; `endpoint` and `property` are one origin, and each requires the other.
ComponentOutputFrom.description: Where the output value comes from.

endpoint.description: Own endpoint whose allocated address property is read.

input.description: Own input forwarded as this output, keeping its sensitivity.

property.description: Address property of the named endpoint.

template.description: String with ${{ self.endpoints.<name>.<property> }} references, substituted once.

ComponentProbe.$comment: spec.md §5.4. The mechanism is the key that is present, as in a Kubernetes probe. HTTP is the only mechanism in v1; another is added as a sibling key.

failureThreshold.description: Consecutive failures required to consider the probe failing.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Seconds to wait after start before the first probe.

successThreshold.description: Consecutive successes required to consider the probe passing.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for a probe response.

cron.$comment: spec.md §5.7. Five fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) separated by one or more spaces or tabs, evaluated in UTC. The field count is structural so a seconds field or an @-macro is rejected rather than read two ways. The grammar and range of each field are a semantic rule of spec.md §5.7 (ERR_INVALID_SCHEDULE).
cron.description: Five-field cron expression, evaluated in UTC, on which the JOB recurs.

ComponentSource.$comment: spec.md §5.1 / ADR 0031 §1. The key that is present says where the image comes from; there is no tag. Exactly one of the two is REQUIRED: neither is a missing field and both an invalid value.

git.description: A Git repository the platform builds into an image.

allOf.$comment: spec.md §5. `type` is the category and selects which fields apply. EXTERNAL is a node this platform does not run: it has no workload, so its inputs have no environment target, and it exists to publish values another node consumes, so an absent contract is a missing field and an empty outputs mapping an invalid value. Written as if/then over properties declared once, so every default beneath stays within the effective-value resolution ADR 0008 requires.
spec.md §5. A SERVICE is request-driven, so it declares at least one endpoint. An absent block is a missing field and an empty one an invalid value.
spec.md §5. A JOB runs to completion: it has nothing to run without a command, and it serves nothing, so it declares no endpoint and no probe. Only a JOB may carry a schedule.

contract.description: The composition contract: typed inputs the component needs and outputs it publishes.

type.description: Category of the node: SERVICE (long-running, request-driven, at least one endpoint), WORKER (long-running, not request-driven; endpoints optional and never public), JOB (runs to completion, once per rollout or on a schedule), or EXTERNAL (not run by this platform).

workload.description: How the platform runs the component: source, command, endpoints, environment, storage and health. Required unless type is EXTERNAL, and forbidden when it is.

minSizeGiB.description: Smallest allocation the component can run with. The blueprint allocates at least this.

mountPath.description: Absolute path where the volume is mounted in the workload.

readOnly.description: True when the volume is mounted read-only.

shared.description: True when every replica mounts the same volume at once. False, the volume attaches to one replica at a time.

command.$comment: spec.md §5. Exec form: each item is one argument and no shell parses them. It replaces the image CMD and keeps its ENTRYPOINT, which is what `command` means in Docker and Compose.
command.description: Arguments the workload runs, as a list, with no shell. Replaces the image CMD and keeps its ENTRYPOINT. Required for a JOB.

endpoints.description: Named ports the workload listens on. Required on a SERVICE, optional on a WORKER (never exposed publicly), forbidden on a JOB.

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §5.2. An endpoint name is referenced by probes, outputs and blueprint exposure, and is composed into a DNS label beside other slugs rather than being one. Alphanumeric keeps any hyphen separator unambiguous; 20 characters leave room in the 63-character label for what it composes with.

additionalProperties.description: Verbatim value. An empty string is allowed.

envVars.description: Intrinsic non-secret environment constants, keyed by variable name. Configurable values are inputs with a target, supplied by the blueprint.

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §5.3 / ADR 0007 §4. The POSIX shape: a name outside it is not portably settable. A duplicate key is rejected by the parser, so no rule here repeats it.

health.description: Staged health probes (startup, readiness, liveness). Omitted when none are defined; forbidden on a JOB.

schedule.description: Makes a JOB recur. Omitted, the job runs once per rollout. Forbidden on every other type.

source.description: Where the workload image comes from: a pinned image, or a Git repository the platform builds.

volumes.description: Persistent storage the workload mounts, with the minimum size each needs.
